title: feat(monitor-scaling): per-monitor scale targeting with layout-safe position recompute
head: 5f2ff384ba5f
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
decision: findings: F1 auto-placed monitors pinned (layout flip, source/model-based), F2 omarchy_monitor_scale shadowed + manual stale, F3 backup per call (More findings)

leads.summary: Rewriting every matching desc: rule also changes another monitor sharing that prefix
leads.consequence: With desc:ACME for two displays and a later eDP-1-specific rule, scaling only eDP-1 also changes the shared desc:ACME rule from 1.5 to 2. DP-2 has no later override and changes to 2 on reload. Hyprland matches desc: by prefix and selects its last matching rule, so this is not merely textual duplication. The fixture shows both rules rewritten; after reload the other display no longer retains its configured scale. Restrict edits to the effective rule, or avoid modifying a desc: rule shared by another connected output.

leads.summary: Appending a named rule converts auto placement into a fixed position across hotplug
leads.consequence: The shipped monitors.lua uses position = auto. Scaling a monitor without its own rule appends a connector-specific rule with the live XxY instead of auto. After unplugging or rearranging another monitor, that output stays at a now-stale explicit coordinate; Hyprland positions explicit outputs first and only auto-places those without a fixed position. For example a secondary initially auto-placed at x=1920 keeps that explicit position when the 1920-logical-pixel primary is replaced by a 2560-logical-pixel one, so the outputs now overlap by 640 pixels instead of the secondary being auto-placed at x=2560. Preserve an auto position for newly appended rules, or explicitly document/handle topology changes.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F1, same mechanism); corroboration

leads.summary: A never-executed Lua branch is treated as the monitor's effective rule
leads.consequence: A valid config with an output-specific rule in `if false then ... end` and an active catch-all causes the awk pass to rewrite the inactive rule, conclude it found a match and omit the appended rule. The command returns success; on reload the active catch-all restores the old scale. The fixture shows the disabled rule changing from 1 to 2 while the catch-all remains 1.5. Do not claim persistence by static matching alone for executable Lua configurations, or verify the effective rule on reload.

leads.summary: The new global GDK max is saved to Lua but not propagated to app-launch environments
leads.consequence: When the max changes, the command writes the new integer only into monitors.lua. A config reload sets Hyprland's own process environment through hl.env but the shipped call passes no third dbus flag, so Hyprland does not update systemd/DBus activation environment. The only --all import is a session-start event. The shell launches gtk-launch via UWSM's default scope, which inherits the already-running shell's old environment; after a scale operation, new apps may still see the old GDK_SCALE until a new session even though the file says the max. An end-to-end fix also has to update systemd/DBus and use a launch path that consumes the new environment, as open #10570 proposes with UWSM's service mode.
leads.triage: pre-existing behaviour (base also only writes the file); dropped as out of PR scope

leads.summary: Open greeter-scale PR #7501 reads the now-unchanged catch-all and erases the per-monitor scale on logout
leads.consequence: #7501 calls its helper with the new scale at scale-change time, but on logout calls it with no argument; that helper resolves the unchanged `omarchy_monitor_scale = "auto" from monitors.lua rather than a named output's scale. Against this PR's default plus its appended 3x output rule, the fixture saves `3` and then overwrites it with `auto` on logout. The greeter no longer follows the adjusted display. If both PRs merge, reconcile the helper with per-monitor persisted rules and choose which display's scale drives the greeter. The shared script has a merge-file conflict that needs explicit resolution.
leads.triage: factual; verified via gh api (#7501 open, helper reads local omarchy_monitor_scale); also confirmed in Opus self-check

leads.summary: Open Display panel PR #13293 invokes an incompatible --monitor CLI
leads.consequence: #13293's panel calls `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-scaling --monitor NAME SCALE`; this PR accepts `SCALE NAME` only. Combining its panel with this CLI makes every selected scale exit 1 with Usage and change neither live nor persisted scale. The two script changes also have merge-file conflict markers, so merging both requires explicitly agreeing on the flag/positional interface and updating the panel and its tests.
leads.triage: factual; verified via gh api diff (args [--monitor NAME], panel calls --monitor)

leads.summary: Single-quoted selectors and valid hl.monitor{...} calls are mistaken for missing rules
leads.consequence: Lua accepts a table-constructor-only function call without parentheses (`hl.monitor{ output = "eDP-1", bitdepth = 10, scale = 1.5 }`), and accepts single-quoted output selectors (`output = 'eDP-1'`). The awk detector requires `hl.monitor(` and its selector parser requires double quotes; each valid form is treated as absent and followed by a second full rule with default fields. Hyprland's last-rule selection then discards the user's 10-bit bitdepth and replaces other settings with defaults on reload. Match both Lua call and quoted-string forms or refuse non-rewritable configs before live application.

leads.summary: Rejected hyprctl eval still persists a scale and returns success
leads.consequence: If hyprctl eval exits 1, this script ignores it, re-reads the unchanged scale, optionally logs scale-divergence, rewrites monitors.lua and returns zero. The user's screen remains unchanged now but next reload picks up the persisted value; callers see success. A failing-eval stub reproduced `script_status=0` with the config changed from 1.5 to 2. Reject failed evals before persisting and assert the failure path in the test stub.
leads.triage: pre-existing (base also ignores eval status); dropped

leads.summary: Backups with second-resolution filenames overwrite the previous backup on successive scale actions
leads.consequence: Two scale actions within one second both copy to the same .bak.<timestamp>; the second overwrites the pristine pre-first-action snapshot. A fixed-date isolated run yielded one backup of the already modified `scale = 2` and the active config at `scale = 3`, losing the initial `scale = 1.5`. Generate a unique path, as the neighboring layout PR #7152 does, or use mktemp, and test rapid consecutive actions.

leads.summary: Manual's shared-scale editing instructions stop applying after first scale action
leads.consequence: The manual tells users to set `local omarchy_monitor_scale = 1.6` or 1 in monitors.lua. After using the scaling hotkey on the shipped catch-all-only configuration, this PR appends a named scale for that output and never updates the shared local. Edits following that manual on the same display then have no effect: Hyprland picks the later named rule. Explain how to edit/remove the per-output rule and when the shared setting still applies.

leads.summary: An in-place rewrite adds a newline to a file that did not end with one
leads.consequence: When a matching rule's input file ends immediately after `})`, awk's `print` emits a newline and cat overwrites the original. A fixture confirms the resulting last byte is 0a. This contradicts byte-preserving rewrite claims but does not change the active rule; preserve the original trailing-newline state if exact preservation matters.

limits: No live Hyprland or actual monitor/hotplug run: display consequences are deduced from the installed Hyprland 0.56.2-4 source and isolated script fixtures.

Cross-PR results are conditional on preserving each submitted PR's behavior through merge conflict resolution. #13293 and #7501 touch the scaling script and produce conflict markers locally, even though GitHub reports each branch currently MERGEABLE against quattro. ## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** With the default `monitors.lua`, rescaling a non-leftmost monitor flips the layout (per Hyprland 0.56.2 source).

### Auto-placed monitors get pinned

The eval and appended rule (`bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-scaling:301,736`) always carry a literal `position`. Hyprland 0.56.2 places explicit outputs before auto ones, so scaling a right-hand external moves the auto laptop to its right. **Impact:** one Super + / press on the right-hand monitor swaps the layout, also after reload.

**Suggested change:** keep `position = "auto"` for monitors that are auto-placed today; recompute only literal positions.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 5f2ff384)</summary>

Reproducer for omacom/omarchy#11854 at 5f2ff384ba5ff10d582151cba750787f057fbf27. Run from the checkout root. Needs bash, jq, gawk and lua 5.4 or later. The first half runs the PR script against a stubbed `hyprctl` and the shipped `config/hypr/monitors.lua`. The second half is a small model of Hyprland 0.56.2 rule lookup and `arrange()` (the source files are named in the script), because the placement itself needs a compositor.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Run from an omarchy checkout at 5f2ff384 (PR #11854 head). Needs bash, jq, gawk, lua 5.4+.
# Shipped default monitors.lua, laptop eDP-1 on the left and external DP-1 on the
# right (both placed by the auto catch-all), DP-1 focused, then the Display
# panel's 1.6 preset (the panel runs `omarchy-hyprland-monitor-scaling 1.6`).
set -euo pipefail
t=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$t"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$t/bin" "$t/home/.config/hypr"
cp config/hypr/monitors.lua "$t/home/.config/hypr/monitors.lua"
cp config/hypr/monitors.lua "$t/before.lua"
cat >"$t/bin/hyprctl" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
case "$1" in
  monitors) printf '%s' '[{"name":"eDP-1","focused":false,"x":0,"y":0,"width":2880,"height":1800,"scale":2,"refreshRate":120,"transform":0,"description":"BOE X","make":"BOE","model":"X","serial":""},{"name":"DP-1","focused":true,"x":1440,"y":0,"width":3840,"height":2160,"scale":2,"refreshRate":60,"transform":0,"description":"Dell U2723QE","make":"Dell","model":"U2723QE","serial":"1"}]' ;;
  eval) printf '%s\n' "$2" >>"$EVAL_LOG" ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x "$t/bin/hyprctl"
HOME="$t/home" XDG_STATE_HOME="$t/state" PATH="$t/bin:$PATH" EVAL_LOG="$t/eval.log" \
  bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-scaling 1.6
echo "eval:     $(cat "$t/eval.log")"
echo "appended: $(tail -n 1 "$t/home/.config/hypr/monitors.lua")"

# Model of Hyprland v0.56.2: hl.monitor() replaces a rule with the same output
# and appends it (MonitorRuleManager.cpp add); a monitor uses the last matching
# named rule, else the first output = "" rule (MonitorRuleManager.cpp get);
# arrange() places explicit positions first, then each auto output at the right
# edge of everything already placed (state/MonitorPositionController.cpp).
cat >"$t/model.lua" <<'LUA'
local mons = { { name = "eDP-1", w = 2880, live = 2 }, { name = "DP-1", w = 3840, live = 2 } }
local rules = {}
hl = { env = function() end, monitor = function(r)
  for i = #rules, 1, -1 do if rules[i].output == r.output then table.remove(rules, i) end end
  rules[#rules + 1] = r
end }
dofile(arg[1])
if arg[2] then for line in io.lines(arg[2]) do assert(load(line))() end end
local placed, auto = {}, {}
for _, m in ipairs(mons) do
  local r
  for i = #rules, 1, -1 do if rules[i].output == m.name then r = rules[i]; break end end
  if not r then for _, c in ipairs(rules) do if c.output == "" then r = c; break end end end
  m.via, m.lw = (r.output == "" and "catch-all" or r.output), math.floor(m.w / (tonumber(r.scale) or m.live) + 0.5)
  local x = tostring(r.position):match("^(-?%d+)x%-?%d+$")
  if x then m.x = tonumber(x); placed[#placed + 1] = m else auto[#auto + 1] = m end
end
for _, m in ipairs(auto) do
  m.x = 0
  for _, p in ipairs(placed) do m.x = math.max(m.x, p.x + p.lw) end
  placed[#placed + 1] = m
end
for _, m in ipairs(mons) do print(string.format("  %-5s x=%-5d width=%-5d rule=%s", m.name, m.x, m.lw, m.via)) end
LUA
echo "Hyprland placement before:";                 lua "$t/model.lua" "$t/before.lua"
echo "Hyprland placement after the eval:";         lua "$t/model.lua" "$t/before.lua" "$t/eval.log"
echo "Hyprland placement after reload or login:";  lua "$t/model.lua" "$t/home/.config/hypr/monitors.lua"
```

```
Hyprland placement after the eval:
```

### `omarchy_monitor_scale` gets shadowed

Super + / and the panel write a per-connector rule, not `omarchy_monitor_scale`. **Impact:** after one press, the `manual/33-monitors.md` edit stops affecting that monitor.

**Suggested change:** document the per-output rule in the manual and PR description.

<details><summary>Reproducer (5f2ff384)</summary>

Reproducer for omacom/omarchy#11854 at 5f2ff384ba5ff10d582151cba750787f057fbf27. Run from the checkout root. Needs bash, jq, gawk and lua 5.4 or later. The rule lookup at the end follows Hyprland 0.56.2 `CMonitorRuleManager::get` (the last rule naming the connector wins; the `output = ""` rule is only a fallback).

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Run from an omarchy checkout at 5f2ff384 (PR #11854 head). Needs bash, jq, gawk, lua 5.4+.
# Shipped default monitors.lua on a single laptop: one Super + / press, then the
# edit manual/33-monitors.md recommends (local omarchy_monitor_scale = 1).
set -euo pipefail
t=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$t"' EXIT
mkdir -p "$t/bin" "$t/home/.config/hypr"
lua_file="$t/home/.config/hypr/monitors.lua"
cp config/hypr/monitors.lua "$lua_file"
cat >"$t/bin/hyprctl" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
case "$1" in
  monitors) printf '%s' '[{"name":"eDP-1","focused":true,"x":0,"y":0,"width":2880,"height":1800,"scale":2,"refreshRate":120,"transform":0,"description":"BOE X","make":"BOE","model":"X","serial":""}]' ;;
  eval) : ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x "$t/bin/hyprctl"
HOME="$t/home" XDG_STATE_HOME="$t/state" PATH="$t/bin:$PATH" bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-scaling up
sed -i 's/^local omarchy_monitor_scale = .*/local omarchy_monitor_scale = 1/' "$lua_file"
grep -n 'omarchy_monitor_scale\|^hl\.monitor' "$lua_file"
# Hyprland v0.56.2 rule lookup (MonitorRuleManager.cpp get): the last rule whose
# output matches the connector wins; the output = "" rule is only a fallback.
cat >"$t/lookup.lua" <<'LUA'
local rules = {}
hl = { env = function() end, monitor = function(r) rules[#rules + 1] = r end }
dofile(arg[1])
local used
for i = #rules, 1, -1 do if rules[i].output == "eDP-1" then used = rules[i]; break end end
if not used then for _, r in ipairs(rules) do if r.output == "" then used = r; break end end end
print(string.format("eDP-1 uses output = %q, scale = %s", used.output, tostring(used.scale)))
LUA
lua "$t/lookup.lua" "$lua_file"
```

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

### One `monitors.lua.bak.<epoch>` file per call

`persist_monitor_scale` copies the file on every call (`:356`), including a repeat of the current value, and never prunes. Two calls within one second write the same name, so the second overwrites the first pre-change backup. **Impact:** `~/.config/hypr` accumulates a backup per keypress.

**Suggested change:** keep one rolling `monitors.lua.bak`, or skip the backup when the rewrite does not change the file.

Reproducer for omacom/omarchy#11854 at 5f2ff384ba5ff10d582151cba750787f057fbf27. Run from the checkout root. Needs bash, jq and gawk.

```bash

# Run from an omarchy checkout at 5f2ff384 (PR #11854 head). Needs bash, jq, gawk.

cp config/hypr/monitors.lua "$t/home/.config/hypr/monitors.lua"
cat >"$t/bin/hyprctl" <<'SH'

  monitors) printf '%s' '[{"name":"eDP-1","focused":true,"x":0,"y":0,"width":2880,"height":1800,"scale":2,"refreshRate":120,"transform":0,"description":"BOE X","make":"BOE","model":"X","serial":""}]' ;;
  eval) : ;;
esac
SH
chmod +x "$t/bin/hyprctl"
for arg in 1.6 1.6 1.25 up; do
  HOME="$t/home" XDG_STATE_HOME="$t/state" PATH="$t/bin:$PATH" bin/omarchy-hyprland-monitor-scaling "$arg"
```
